Corked green bottles and snail-shell cups packed four deep beside a long-necked decanter whose rose-gold liquid pours endlessly upward, and a squat jar where a seedling sprouts, flowers, and seeds again in a slow emerald loop, every shell cup sealed in violet wax stamped with a painted crescent, one decanter weighted under a smooth river stone.

Hand-blown phials and stoppered gourds crowding a beeswax tin shelf, one ruby phial holding a single bright fish swimming lazy figure-eights, another a bottle of night sky with real cold stars drifting inside it, each gourd tied with ochre-dyed thread, the star-bottle's blue glow spilling across the plain timber of its neighbour's blank surface.

Woven-willow boxes and amber corked bottles wedged around a bell-jar of luminous jellyfish-caps drifting in slow sapphire, beside a phial holding only pure gold colour, weightless and clear, each box tied with a dried lavender sprig tucked under brown twine, one phial standing in a saucer of water because it runs too warm to shelve.

Squat stoneware pots and birch-bark cylinders crowded two deep around a stoppered flask where green flame burns underwater in unmoving emerald silence, and a tall bottle of snowflakes held forever mid-tumble in pale silver air, each pot ringed in dyed indigo thread, the flask's green light casting soft colour across every plain surface beside it.

Acorn-cup measures and hand-blown turquoise phials jostling a corked bottle where will-o-wisps cluster gold and restless at the shoulder, beside a jar holding one tiny full moon sealed behind glass, its white light steady and cold, every phial sealed in green wax pressed with a painted leaf, one cork straining visibly against something urgent within.

Pinch-bowls and hooped firkins packed tight beside a long-necked bottle of captured dawn, its apricot and rose light warming the whole row, and a jar of slow gold spores drifting inside it like slow snow, each firkin tagged with a small blank scrap of birch-bark tied at the handle, one bowl mended along its cracks with bright gold.

Stoppered gourds and squat emerald-glazed pots crowded around a phial where a tiny perfect rose opens and closes in deep ruby rhythm, beside a bottle of moonlight with a blue-white luminescence that brightens as the room grows dark, each gourd sealed in cream wax with a painted spiral, the moonlight bottle's glow lighting all its neighbours to silver.

Bell-jar and corked amber bottles surrounded by woven-willow boxes, the bell-jar holding a small thunderstorm with a violet fork of lightning alive inside it, one amber bottle carrying a seven-banded potion in emerald, sapphire, ruby, gold, rose, amethyst and white, each box tied with a dried rosemary sprig, the bell-jar frosting the plain timber directly beneath it white.

Hand-blown phials and birch-bark cylinders wedged around a beeswax tin, one phial a bottled sea-storm with dark indigo water churning in miniature inside, another holding a single trill of birdsong visible as a bright gold ripple circling the glass endlessly, each cylinder left entirely plain, one phial with a tiny hinged copper shutter to dim its restless amber glow.

Snail-shell cups and a long-necked decanter packed beside squat stoneware pots, the decanter filled with bottled sunset layered in amber and burnt rose that shifts and bleeds slowly, one pot holding a jar of held breath with pearl mist turning in a slow interior spiral, every shell cup sealed in red wax with a small painted flame.

Corked green bottles and acorn-cup measures crowded three deep around a phial where seeds hang perfectly motionless in mid-air inside clear glass, and a squat jar of coiled green lightning that pulses against its stoneware sides, each bottle twine-tied with a dried berry cluster tucked under the string, the lightning jar's light spilling sharp and restless onto plain timber below.

Woven-willow boxes and hand-blown sapphire phials surrounding a hooped firkin, one phial containing warm rain falling forever on a thimble of bright moss in endless soft patter, another a bottle of will-o-wisps in gold and pale green pressing the glass, each box sealed in blue wax with a painted star, one firkin weighted under a flat grey stone.

Beeswax tins and stoppered gourds wedged around a bell-jar where captured fireflies light the entire bay in warm gold, beside a long-necked bottle where a tiny full autumn tree has grown inside and turned every leaf copper, each tin tied with crimson-dyed thread, the firefly jar's glow warm enough to cast shadows behind every plain vessel behind it.

Birch-bark cylinders and pinch-bowls jostling corked amber bottles, one bottle holding bottled moonlight with a cold silver luminescence, another an hourglass-shaped vessel whose glowing pollen-sand hangs in a slow amber cloud instead of running, each cylinder left plain, one pinch-bowl once cracked clean through and mended with gold along every seam.

Squat stoneware pots and snail-shell cups crowded beside a hand-blown ruby phial where a green flame burns in absolute stillness beneath clear liquid, and a tall corked bottle of night sky with tiny real stars that drift and occasionally cross, each pot sealed in black wax with a painted crescent moon, one phial too warm to shelve standing in a chipped saucer.

Acorn-cup measures and woven-willow boxes packed around a long-necked decanter of bottled dawn in layered apricot and pale gold, beside a phial holding only light, pure turquoise colour, each box tied with a dried chamomile sprig under rough twine, the decanter's warm light touching every plain timber surface in the row to copper.

Corked green and amber bottles crowded two and three deep around a stoppered gourd, one bottle a seven-banded potion whose colours shift order if watched patiently, another a phial where warm rain falls in perpetual silver threads onto a scrap of living emerald moss, each bottle plain-surfaced, one gourd sealed in yellow wax stamped with a painted bee.

Hand-blown phials and hooped firkins wedged beside a beeswax tin, one phial of bottled sunset bleeding rose into amber in slow tidal motion, another a jar where a single bright fish swims steady turquoise laps in water kept always in motion, each firkin ringed in green-dyed thread, one phial's glow visibly brightening as the lamplight across the room is dimmed.

Pinch-bowls and birch-bark cylinders surrounding a corked ruby bottle of will-o-wisps clustered warm and restless at the shoulder, beside a bell-jar holding luminous jellyfish-caps in pale sapphire drifting slow and unhurried, each bowl sealed in orange wax with a painted sprig of holly, one cylinder with a tiny hinged shutter of hammered tin fitted to dim the jellyfish glow.

Stoneware pots and woven-willow boxes crowded around a long-necked bottle of bottled moonlight, its silver-white light steady and cold, beside a phial of coiled green lightning behind glass that flares and dims in long slow pulses, each pot tagged with a small blank scrap of birch-bark, the moonlight bottle having frosted a pale ring into the plain timber beneath it.

Snail-shell cups and acorn-cup measures jostling corked green bottles, one bottle holding snowflakes held spinning in slow white suspension inside deep blue-tinted glass, another a jar of gold spores falling through amber air in soft unending snow, each shell cup sealed in purple wax with a tiny painted spiral, one heavy bottle weighted down by a round river stone.

Hand-blown phials and stoppered gourds packed beside a beeswax tin, one phial a bottled sea-storm with dark water cresting against emerald-lit glass, another a jar where a rose opens and closes in deep ruby, its petals spreading and furling in an unbroken twelve-second rhythm, each phial twine-tied with a dried fern frond, the sea-storm phial lit from within bright as a lantern.

Hooped firkins and birch-bark cylinders crowded around a bell-jar where captured fireflies drift gold, lighting the bay amber-warm, beside a corked bottle holding a small thunderstorm with a real blue-white fork of lightning crossing the interior glass again and again, each firkin sealed in dark wax with a painted moon, one cylinder so cold it has silvered with frost.

Corked amber bottles and woven-willow boxes surrounding a long-necked decanter of held breath, pearl-white mist turning in a slow interior coil, and a phial of birdsong ripple in bright gold circling the glass, each bottle ringed in rose-dyed thread, one box long ago broken and mended in gold along every crack so it catches and scatters light across the row.

Pinch-bowls and squat stoneware pots wedged around hand-blown phials, one phial holding seeds hanging perfectly motionless in mid-air inside clear glass, another a stoppered bottle of night sky with cold real stars slow-drifting through absolute darkness behind the glass, each pot sealed in red wax with a painted berry cluster, one phial standing in a small saucer of water, too warm to shelve.
